title: C06 The City Between
body:
### Campaign Frame

#### The Pitch
This underwater-themed campaign takes place in and around Tidecrown, a unique surface-level city located in the northern Thunder Sea, equidistant from Sarlona and Khorvaire. It serves as a diplomatic hub between aquatic and non-aquatic cultures in Eberron. The setting explores themes of civilization, exploitation, eldritch horror, and awakening truth.

#### Themes
- **Hidden Atrocities** – Civilization hides cruelty under polished diplomacy.
- **Cosmic Horror** – The Deep One/Shargon hybrid is not magic-born, but summoned by collective belief.
- **Moral Dilemmas** – No faction is wholly “right” — alliances are situational and fragile.
- **Ancient Guardianship** – The Couaxolotl once upheld the balance, now nearly extinct.
- **Sacred Relics** – The prismatic pearls are both legendary power sources and the key to sealing the Overlord.

#### Touchstones
- Atlantis (Greek myth)
- John C. Lilly (LSD and dolphins) 
- Avatar (James Cameron movie series)
- Princess Mononoke (movie)
- Adventure Zone: Ethersea
- Deep Ones of H.P. Lovecraft
- **To watch for visual inspiration**: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou (2004), The Abyss (1989), Atlantis: The Lost Empire (2001), Aquaman (2018), Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom (2023), Avatar: The Way of Water (2022), Finding Nemo (2003), Underwater (2020)

### Player Characters
- **[[Maris Wavedeep]]** (female Merfolk Fathomless Warlock). Played by Alex. Thinks she's a cleric, but actually has an aboleth patron. From the Northern Sea region, with some connection to the Aboleth Temple in that region. She's tied to Tidecrown by a divine mission to be an ambassador/prophet to share the good news. Belief has changed her for the better. She has a friend (another prophet) who she arrived with - two by two! Stops by Lotor's food stall every morning, and tells him about the good news. He listens closely and just says "maybe next time".
- **[[Cordelia]]** (female Sea Elf Circle of the Sea Druid). Played by Kerrie. Belongs to an offshoot clan to the Valraean Protectorate from the deeper sea (Dark Sea region), with more of a focus on protection of nature. Secretly fears that she won't be able to protect the deep on her own. Tied to Tidecrown by her zealotry to communicate the importance of the deep and how it can't just be mined for resources. Her mother, Lydia, is her former mentor who she aspires to become - she died recently. She has scheduled sparring sessions with Ghomuth - they know each other from before they both got to the base, and are from the same general area of the sea.
- **[[Lotor Sphinx]]** (male Human Life Domain Cleric). Played by Trey. "Cast iron chef" who wants to start a food stand on the base. Wife died, and his son ran away (so he doesn't know where he is). Most law enforcement don't trust him, but the everyday people do (gives out food in exchange for lodging). Believes that something better can always happen the next day - no matter how bad this one was. Friends with Tessira Vane, who helps advertise his business to her customers. Maris stops by the food stall every morning, and tells Lotor about the good news - he listens closely and just says "maybe next time".
- **[[Ghomuth]]** (male Locathah Zealot Barbarian). Played by Sara. Bodyguard for hire, but only for other locathah (and is currently protecting the head necromancy cleric of the locathah - Velim). She came to Tidecrown because of slavery - she's here to confront those who are involved (both the sahuagin for locathah directly and the Tidecrown people for the kuo-toa). Only trusts her fellow locathah, and would risk anything for them. Fears that her civilization will be wiped out. Has scheduled sparring session with Cordelia - they know each other from before they both got to the base, and are from the same general area (Dark Sea).
- **[[Christopher Pine]]** (male Human Artillerist Artificer). 
- **[[Glooglugogg (Glu)]]** (male Kuo-toa Arcane Trickster Rogue). Born on the base, and a laborer, who sometimes just takes stuff while working. He is trusted (in a limited capacity given his station) by the magewrights who run the actual equipment (engineers), but not trusted by the general population of the base. Secretly fears that things won't get better in the deep (slavery forever).
	- Glu died at the claws of a few chuul outside of the Aboleth Temple, only a few weeks into the campaign.

#### NPCs Connected to PCs
- **Ermias** (male Dwarf Merchant). A merchant who helped Lotor with his re-entry into society after getting out of prison. Lotor saved him during the raid at which Lotor was arrested, allowing Ermias to get away. He never totally left the criminal scene though, and now serves as a fence for Mith - helping out in his theft.
- **Chief Gregaarious Lonadar** (male Gnome Magewright, Chief Engineer). The primary engineer who keeps the base afloat, and who Glu works with routinely. Has a haughty voice, and is as pedantic as possible. All of the kuo-toa workers pronounce his wrong (as "gregarious"), and he's constantly correcting them.
- **Nautia** (female Triton Missionary). Maris's fellow missionary and prophet, who arrived to Tidecrown with her.
- **Lydia** (female Sea Elf Druid). Clio's former mentor, and mother (who died very recently), who she aspires to become.
- **Velim** (male Locathah Cleric). Head cleric (necromancer and follower of Eadro) of the locathah, who is being protected by Ghomuth during his visit to Tidecrown - where he intends to confront the city's leaders about their use of forced labor.
- **Tessira Vane** (CG female Half-Elf Shopkeeper, Pearl Market merchant). Helps advertise Lotor's business to her customers.

### Session Structure ([[Open Table Campaigns|Open Table]])
- Every session begins and ends in Tidecrown. Characters may rotate in and out without explanation.
- Each session opens with a brief, matter-of-fact **morning briefing** delivered by a reliable organizational contact. The briefing is informational, not prescriptive: it surfaces what has changed, what has been noticed, and what is currently possible. When the briefing ends, the players choose what they want to pursue.
- Travel is handled as narration and planning, then resolved through the engagement roll. Return travel is assumed and never rolled.

### Outline

#### Act 1 — The Breach in the Peace (Sessions 1–2)
- **Session Start:** Morning briefing at the PCs’ organization in Tidecrown on the day of the diplomatic summit. The murder, summit tension, and other current pressures are presented as status items. The PCs decide what they want to pursue.
- **Inciting Event:** The night before the diplomatic summit, a Sea Elf envoy is found murdered in their private quarters. The scene is ritualistic — strange runes daubed in fish oil, concentric saltwater rings, black pearls in the victim’s eyes.
- **Political Situation:**
    - Sea Elves demand justice before talks begin.
    - Sahuagin are accused, furious at being blamed before they arrive.
    - Tidecrown leaders want a neutral party to investigate quietly; whether the PCs take this on is their choice. If they don’t, the city will act anyway, and the political consequences will escalate.
- **B-Plot Seed:** Dr. Lilly Fellwater’s prized kuo-toa subject escaped last night (the night before the summit, right after the sea elf envoy murder). Rumors/evidence suggest its behavior matches the killer’s methods.
- **Act 1 End Trigger:** PCs leave Tidecrown following leads into the Thunder Sea.

#### Act 2 — The Depths Awaken (Majority of Campaign)
- PCs explore the Thunder Sea pointcrawl, meeting factions and uncovering pieces of both mysteries:
    1. **The murder** (and the escaped kuo-toa).
    2. **The slow emergence** of the Overlord.
- **Factions** will react dynamically to PC actions. Should take one faction turn per session - choosing either a faction the PCs interacted with that week, or choosing one at random.
- **Pearls** appear organically — not fixed locations — and grant fixed boons (see below).

##### Beat 1: Kuo-Toa Ruins
- **Location.** [[1-06 Dark Sea#⚔4 Kuo-toa Settlement/Ruins]]
- **What the players learn.** The history of the severance, the cult's presence, and that the Pilgrim left recently with purpose — he was asking about ancient Sarlonan traders his people encountered before the severance.
- **Clue 1:** Ssiveth recalls the Pilgrim asking about objects the coastal Sarlonans left behind in the sea.
- **Clue 2:** A carved fragment in the cult space depicts a bowl held over dreaming figures — older than the cult's presence, predating the settlement.
- **Clue 3:** A convert who stayed behind describes the Pilgrim speaking of "the vessel the drowned people guard without knowing it."

##### Beat 2: Aventi Ruins
- **Location:** A drowned pre-Inspired city on the seafloor off the Aventus Islands. The sentira bowl sits in a collapsed communal dreaming hall at the deepest intact level. [[1-04 Barren Sea#✣11 Aventi Ruins]]
- **Entry hook:** The Aventi have oral tradition pointing here but won't retrieve the bowl themselves — their history calls it dangerous. Ganelle will share the location after negotiation, not freely.
- **Challenge:** **Sea spawn and deep scions** fill the upper ruins — former Aventi explorers transformed by prolonged exposure to the bowl's psychic bleed. A **brain coral** colony has grown around the bowl itself and defends it if removal is attempted.
- **Clue 1:** Ganelle, told the bowl is gone, says her people's oral tradition warns it was meant to be used "where the old door stood" — a place in open ocean her ancestors marked on charts that no longer exist.
- **Clue 2:** The dreaming hall's star maps show a marked location in open water — no landmark, no feature, just a position cross-referenced against a sky that includes Crya. A DC 14 History check confirms the notation marks a former planar contact point.
- **Clue 3:** A deep scion, if communicated with rather than killed, repeats fragmented Aquan: _"where the water forgets how to dream."_

##### Beat 3: Dal Quor Scar
- **Location:** An unremarkable stretch of open ocean with nothing to mark it — except navigation feels slightly wrong, dreaming creatures avoid it, and the water has an ashen quality. This is where Dal Quor was last coterminous before the severance. No faction knows what it is. [[1-02 Northern Sea#⚔1 Dal Quor Scar]]
- **What the Pilgrim does here:** Uses the bowl to facilitate collective dreaming outward, re-opening the scar just enough to confirm the door can be widened. He leaves minutes before the players arrive.
- **What the players find:** The water is changed — a faint, unstable proto-manifest zone flickers where there was nothing. Cult members remain, disoriented and mid-vision. The bowl's impression remains in the sediment.
- **Challenge:** The newly-opened scar draws strange creatures from the plane of dreams itself - various quori.
- **Clue 1:** A surviving cult member says the Pilgrim spoke of one remaining step — "the machine that holds the door closed" — and that it lies in the giants' drowned land to the south.
- **Clue 2:** The proto-manifest zone produces a shared involuntary vision in any creature remaining 10 minutes: Giant ruins on the ocean floor, a vast mechanism still turning, a sky without a thirteenth moon.
- **Clue 3:** A deep scion present at the scar, if communicated with, repeats fragmented Giant astronomical notation — the same script from the Aventi dreaming hall, now pointing south toward Xen'drik.

##### Beat 4: Moon Breaker Site
- **Location:** A submerged Sul'at Giant facility, mostly collapsed but with the machine's core intact — still running at low idle, maintaining the severance. The surrounding water suppresses psychic and dream activity. Navigation is subtly wrong. Nothing lives here voluntarily. [[1-04 Barren Sea#⚔3 Moon Breaker Site]]
- **Challenge:** The machine has trapped psychic entities that pressed through the severed gate over millennia and got stuck. **Intellect devourers** and **star spawn** reskinned as crystallized dream-fragments defend the core. Proximity to the machine forces Wisdom saves against a confusion effect.
- **The confrontation:** The Pilgrim is here, bowl in hand, mid-ritual. This is the first time the players can actually reach him. He doesn't fight — he talks, tells them plainly what was done to his people, and escapes before the players can stop him. What he's done to the machine is not immediately reversible. The kuo-toa clock advances.
- **Clue 1:** The Pilgrim's parting words reference "the place beneath your home, where the first door was." Cryptic but directional.
- **Clue 2:** The machine's partial damage produces a Dal Quor flicker that Naqaris feels from Tidecrown — Vos's next briefing notes unusual activity at the Couaxolotl Shrine.
- **Clue 3:** Kuo-toa spiral motifs appear among Tidecrown's labor population within days. Vos notes it with procedural calm that signals it's serious.

##### Beat 5: Tidecrown / Couaxolotl Shrine
- **What this is:** A pivot, not a dungeon. Naqaris speaks openly for the first time. The players learn what completing the inversion actually releases — not just Dal Quor reconnected, but forty thousand years of pressure from the other side of the door, and the Deep One is what's been doing the pressing.
- **The reframe:** The Pilgrim is not wrong about the atrocity committed against his people. He is wrong about what comes through with the restoration. This is the moral weight the campaign has been building toward.
- **The endgame becomes visible:** The Abyssal Trench entrance is accessible from the Shrine. The Pilgrim is descending. The players now know where he's going and why.

#### Act 3 — The Sea Devours (Final Arc)
- Faction clocks have advanced significantly, especially the kuo-toa (leading to the emergence of the Deep One).
- PCs decide whether to:
    - Unite factions to seal the Overlord.
    - Back a single faction for dominance.
    - Let chaos reign.
- Final confrontation possible only with sufficient pearls (players can attempt without, but the odds are dire).

#### B-Plot: The Escaped Kuo-toa
- Escaped from Fellwater’s lab the night of the murder.
- Displays unnatural intelligence, repeating phrases in multiple tongues.
- Visions from the Deep One drive its actions.
- Is the true killer of the Sea Elf envoy — but this fact should be discovered only after significant exploration and faction interaction.
- Sightings can occur in any location, letting you steer players toward interesting points in the crawl.
- Treat this as a roaming pressure: it can intersect any session goal, not only murder investigation.

### [[Factions]] and NPCs
- **Dr. Lilly Fellwater** (CN female merfolk scholar, animal behaviorist). Slender, with skin the pale blue of deep glacial ice and hair braided into long cords tipped with tiny glass beads that chime softly when she moves. Always smells faintly of kelp and saltwater tinctures. Obsessive about her kuo-toa research, fiercely protective of her “subjects.”
- **Primarch Tethys Aquarius** (LN female merfolk, Tidecrown’s leader). Tall and regal, with a flowing silver-and-black cape that sways in the water like ink in a current. Her eyes are a striking pale gold, and she never blinks while speaking. Keeps Tidecrown stable at any cost, even through suppression of truth.
- **Envoy Seravel Lorael** (LN female sea elf, diplomat — murder victim). Graceful, with skin patterned in faint turquoise scales and hair bound in coral pins. Known for her clear, cutting voice, like glass struck by a wave. Outspoken critic of sahuagin aggression.
- **Commander Vorthak ir’Ssar** (LE male sahuagin war captain, summit delegate). Broad-shouldered with jagged fin crests dyed crimson, and a deep scar running across his snout. Wears shark-tooth necklaces that clack ominously when he moves. Proud, quick to take offense, respects strength above diplomacy.
- **The Pilgrim** (unaligned kuo-toa, escaped subject). Gaunt, with mottled grey-green skin and bulbous eyes that never quite focus in the same direction. Carries a crude net festooned with shells carved into spirals. Murderer of the sea elf envoy; moves erratically across the Thunder Sea.
- **Naqaris** (NG Couaxolotl, ancient celestial). Massive, axolotl-like body covered in shimmering, iridescent scales. Gills flare like blooming flowers when it speaks, and its voice reverberates like a distant tide. Holds the history of the prismatic pearls.
- **Tessira Vane** (CG female half-elf shopkeeper, Pearl Market merchant). Freckled from sun exposure, with a shock of white hair dyed with streaks of sea-green. Always wears a heavy leather apron with pockets full of coins, shells, and curious trinkets. Gossip hub, knows the rhythms of Tidecrown commerce.
- **Karrun Deepwake** (LN male merfolk healer, Tidecrown Infirmary). Broad chest and muscular arms, scales a deep cobalt blue; wears a necklace of driftwood charms. Left fin is scarred and partially torn, making his swim slightly lopsided. Treats everyone equally, quietly concerned about strange injuries on locals.
- **Sergeant Caelis Dorn** (NE male triton, Tidecrown security). Weathered face with one cloudy, milky-white eye; armor inlaid with tarnished silver wave motifs. Speaks in a gravelly monotone, as if every word costs effort. Oversees city guard rotations, known for “getting results” by any means necessary.
- **Zoril** (N male locathah cartographer). Zoril is small even for a locathah, with patchy, scar-paled scales and one damaged fin bound with copper wire to keep it rigid while swimming. He carries his maps etched into thin shell plates strung together like a flipbook and compulsively reorders them whenever the currents change. He avoids eye contact, refuses to give distances in straight lines, and insists on being paid in coin _and_ a piece of new information, however trivial.
- **The Omnipus** (N male octopus). A huge octopus with an incredible intelligence due to its nine large brains (one in its head and one in each of its tentacles). Each tentacle brain holds all of the details of one of the oceans of Eberron (minus the Bitter Sea and Iceflow Sea, which aren't used in this campaign), and his head holds any information about the land.
- **The Deep One**. An emergent Overlord, formed entirely through worship and belief. A threat to the balance between land and sea, surface and deep.

#### Tidecrown Port Authority & Compact for Trade (PACT)
- PACT is a permanent civic institution chartered by Tidecrown’s ruling council to manage external pressures without binding the city to any single power. Its mandate is deliberately broad: trade disputes, recovery operations, containment of dangerous artifacts, deniable crisis response, and coordination between rival interests operating in or around Tidecrown.
- PACT has no standing military force and no ideological agenda. It survives by coordination, contracts, and information control. Dragonmarked Houses, foreign governments, mercantile interests, and independent actors all work through PACT when neutrality matters or attribution is undesirable. This makes it indispensable—and quietly resented.
- For player characters, PACT functions as infrastructure. It provides information, access, and legitimacy, but never directives. It does not tell the PCs what must be done, only what is currently true and what pressures are emerging. If the players do nothing, PACT continues to act through other channels, and the world moves on.
- PACT is also the custodial authority for hazardous materials recovered in the course of operations, including Prismatic Pearls. Such items are always vaulted and transferred to specialized handlers; they are never retained by field operatives.
- **Magister Ilren Vos** (TN female human, Senior Coordinator, External Operations). Ilren Vos delivers the standing morning briefing at the start of each session. Her briefings are factual, neutral, and non-prescriptive. She presents developments as status updates rather than calls to action, outlining constraints, uncertainties, and observed changes without assigning priority or judgment. Vos is reliable, informed, and deliberately noncommittal. She answers questions precisely but never speculates unless pressed. If her tone shifts from procedural calm to concern, it signals a genuine escalation in the world state.

#### Merfolk of Tidecrown
- **Colors**: kelp green, slate/stone gray, and storm-sky blue
- Mediators, but suppress inconvenient truths (especially about kuo-toa treatment). Can grant access to diplomatic channels and archives.
- **Goal:** Maintain Tidecrown as neutral diplomatic hub (no agenda).
- **Stats** (8): Force 1, Cunning 0, Wealth, 3, Influence 4
- **Assets**:
	- Tidecrown (+2 Wealth, Defense 5)
	- PACT: Port Authority & Compact for Trade (+2 Influence)
- **Relationships**:
	- Sahuagin: –1 (Unfriendly) - Ongoing friction, tolerated only to preserve neutrality and trade stability.
	- Sea Elves: 0 (Indifferent) - Respectful but strained; sea elves doubt Tidecrown’s resolve.
	- Locathah: +1 (Friendly) - Quiet coexistence and mutual reliance.
	- Kuo-toa: –1 (Unfriendly) - Official denial masking discomfort and exploitation.
	- Couaxolotl: +1 (Friendly) - Seen as mythic allies and stabilizing forces.
	- Aventi: 0 (Indifferent) - Occasional trade, no formal position.

#### Sahuagin (Eternal Dominion)
- **Colors**: black (abyssal depth), blood-red (conflict/victory), and deep green. These colors represent their tripartite social structure, and are often presented in a “threefold maw” or triskelion-like pattern.
- The sahuagin are not merely raiders; they are a predatory civilization that believes dominance is the natural moral order. Strength is proof of truth, and weakness is consent. While divided into rival clans, they share a religious cosmology centered on Sha’argon and the idea that the Thunder Sea exists to be culled, ruled, and consumed. Diplomacy is tolerated only as a delay tactic; coexistence is a lie they believe others tell themselves.
- They are acutely aware that the world is changing. The strange tides, the altered creatures, and the dreams spreading among lesser peoples all confirm what their priests have long preached: the sea is awakening, and those strong enough to ride that awakening will inherit it. The sahuagin intend to be those inheritors.
- The sahuagin dwell on the floor of the Thunder Sea. They possess an uncanny ability to rapidly adapt to changing pressure, and can ascend from the depths to the surface with no ill effects. 
- **Goal**: Establish unquestioned religious and military dominance of the Thunder Sea.
- **Stats** (8): Force 4, Cunning 2, Wealth 1, Influence 1
- **Assets**:
	- Leviathan Warbands (+2 Force, Defense 2)
	- Blood-Priesthood of Shargon (+2 Influence)
	- Slave Infrastructure (+1 Wealth)
- **Relationships**:
	- PCs / Tidecrown: –1 (Unfriendly) - Viewed as weak mediators sheltering prey.
	- Sea Elves: –2 (Hostile) - Ancient, irreconcilable enemies.
	- Locathah: –2 (Hostile) - Considered property, not a people.
	- Kuo-toa: –1 (Unfriendly) - Useful omens, dangerous instability.
	- Couaxolotl: –2 (Hostile) - Mythic enemies obstructing destiny.
	- Aventi: –1 (Unfriendly) - Scavengers trespassing in claimed waters.
- **Agenda** (8):
	 - [x] Denunciation of Tidecrown neutrality (Portent: Sahuagin emissaries openly defy diplomatic norms) ✅ 2026-03-16
	 - [ ]  Coordinated peripheral raids (Portent: Multiple trade routes report synchronized attacks)
	 - [ ]  Expansion of priestly rites (Portent: Chanting currents carry for miles)
	 - [ ]  Clan unification under shared symbols (Portent: Warbands display identical markings)
	 - [ ]  Seizure of deep sacred zones (Portent: A kar’lassa region becomes violently unstable)
	 - [ ]  Declaration of divine mandate (Portent: Public ritual killings circulate symbolically)
	 - [ ]  Total military mobilization (Portent: Armed patrols dominate neutral waters)
	 - [ ]  Open holy war (Portent: Borders collapse across the sea)

#### Sea Elves (Valraean Protectorate)
- **Colors**: pearl (Undying Court), bright teal (Aerenal waters), and sun-gold (Irian/positive energy association)
- The sea elves are a power that mistakes restraint for virtue and order for justice. They see themselves as custodians of maritime stability, heirs to ancient compacts that predate Tidecrown entirely. To them, sahuagin aggression is not a moral outrage so much as a strategic inevitability that must be contained before it spreads.
- What truly threatens them is erosion of legitimacy. If the sea elves cannot enforce norms, patrol borders, and punish transgression, then their authority becomes ceremonial. The envoy’s murder is therefore existential: a test of whether diplomacy still has teeth, or whether the age of treaties is ending.
- **Goal**: Preserve regional stability (especially around their Aerenal territory) by containing sahuagin expansion.
- **Stats** (8): Force 2, Cunning 1, Wealth 2, Influence 3
- **Assets**:
	- Valraean Patrol Fleets (+2 Force, Defense 2)
	- Diplomatic Accords (+2 Influence)
	- Aereni Supply Lines (+1 Wealth)
- **Relationships**:
	- PCs / Tidecrown: 0 (Indifferent) - Necessary partner, unreliable enforcer.
	- Sahuagin: –2 (Hostile) - Existential threat requiring containment.
	- Locathah: 0 (Indifferent) - Seen as non-actors, neither allies nor threats.
	- Kuo-toa: –1 (Unfriendly) - Unpredictable and dangerous.
	- Couaxolotl: +1 (Friendly) - Shared ancient knowledge and aligned goals.
	- Aventi: 0 (Indifferent) - Historical curiosity, no trust or hostility.
- **Agenda** (8):
	 - [x] Demand formal justice for the envoy (Portent: Sea elf banners withdraw from cooperative ports) ✅ 2026-05-25
	 - [ ]  Expansion of patrol zones (Portent: Civilian traffic faces inspections)
	 - [ ]  Political pressure on Tidecrown (Portent: Trade partners receive quiet warnings)
	 - [ ]  Intelligence gathering on sahuagin rites (Portent: Sea elf agents appear far from home)
	 - [ ]  Fleet-scale readiness drills (Portent: Military maneuvers dominate the horizon)
	 - [ ]  Containment strikes (Portent: A sahuagin site is destroyed without explanation)
	 - [ ]  Coalition negotiations (Portent: External navies enter talks)
	 - [ ]  End of neutrality doctrine (Portent: Sea elves claim enforcement authority)

##### Abyssal Protectorate
- **Colors**: pearl (Undying Court), deep blue (deep and dark waters), and sun-gold (Irian/positive energy association)
- These sea elves split from the main faction because they could not justify the oppressive rule of the Valraeans, though they aren't without lingering traces of arrogance at times. The Abyssal Protectorate are smaller in numbers but are each responsible for a fairly large patch of the deep in the Thunder Sea. They strive to protect the natural way of the ocean and dedicate their lives to it, even if it means living a relatively isolated life in darkness to do so.
- Recently, the dragonmarked houses have become eager to explore the ocean floor for Siberys dragonshards. Not only would this affect the life of the fish and animals in the deep, but boring in the ocean floor may also disturb the boundary between the surface and Khyber. This is specifally a joint effort between House Cannith and House Lyrandar, which are creating deep sea mining equipment and using elemental submarines to get there.

#### Locathah
- **Colors**: tan (maps and sand), light blue (sea water), kelp green (underwater and necromancy)
- Locathah are subjects of both the Valraean Protectorate and the eastern regions of the Eternal Dominion. The locathah never had a civilization as advanced as the sahuagin, and have been subjects of the Dominion for thousands of years.
- The locathah are not a resistance movement, and they do not wish to become one. They are a people defined by endurance, adaptation, and deliberate invisibility. Their philosophy is simple: survive quietly, avoid entanglement, and let the currents carry conflict elsewhere. Unfortunately, this has made them ideal targets for exploitation.
- They know the sea better than anyone. They map currents, remember safe passages, and observe shifts in water, predator behavior, and political borders long before others notice. Their tragedy is that knowledge without power invites abuse. They will not revolt unless forced, and even then they will fracture rather than unite openly.
- **Goal**: Continue living peacefully without being drawn into open conflict.
- **Stats** (6): Force 0, Cunning 3, Wealth 2, Influence 1
- **Assets**:
	- Hidden Current Routes (+2 Cunning)
	- Cartographer Elders (+1 Influence)
	- Trade-Bound Labor Pools (+1 Wealth)
- **Relationships**:
	- PCs / Tidecrown: +1 (Friendly) - Provides relative safety and non-interference.
	- Sahuagin: –2 (Hostile) - Oppressors and enslavers.
	- Sea Elves: 0 (Indifferent) - Powerful but distant.
	- Kuo-toa: 0 (Indifferent) - Shared marginalization, no coordination.
	- Couaxolotl: 0 (Indifferent) - Revered, but remote and abstract.
	- Aventi: +1 (Friendly) - Mutual displacement and quiet cooperation.
- **Agenda** (6):
	 - [ ]  Withdrawal from contested waters (Portent: Locathah fishing grounds quietly relocate)
	 - [ ]  Expansion of neutral travel corridors (Portent: Ships report unusually smooth passage)
	 - [ ]  Increased information exchange with outsiders (Portent: Accurate rumors spread without attribution)
	 - [ ]  Negotiation of informal protections (Portent: Locathah intermediaries appear in neutral ports)
	 - [ ]  Consolidation into safer enclaves (Portent: Entire communities vanish from old maps)
	 - [ ]  Cultural preservation over territory (Portent: Locathah refuse to take sides publicly)

- Player use: The locathah are the best navigational and intelligence resource in the campaign, precisely because they refuse to weaponize that knowledge themselves.

#### Kuo-toa
- **Colors**: deep indigo (Dal Quor), silver (contrast representing lucidity), violet/purple (accent representing unstable thought)
- The kuo-toa are not consciously raising the Overlord. They are remembering something the world tried to forget. Their minds resonate with pressure, depth, and dream, and as the sea changes, so do they. Each shared vision sharpens their awareness; each ritual makes the impossible more real.
- Unlike other factions, they do not plan. Their agenda represents collective awakening rather than strategy. The more aware they become, the more visible the Overlord becomes to everyone else.
- **Goal**: Give form and meaning to the visions rising from the deep.
- **Stats** (6): Force 1, Cunning 1, Wealth 0, Influence 4
- **Assets**:
	- Dreaming Congregations (+2 Influence)
	- Ancestral Deep Ruins (+1 Cunning, Defense 1)
	- The Pilgrim (+2 Influence)
- Relationships:
	- PCs / Tidecrown: –1 (Unfriendly) - Fear, control, and exploitation.
	- Sahuagin: –1 (Unfriendly) - Resented predators, half-mythologized.
	- Sea Elves: –1 (Unfriendly) - Seen as distant enforcers.
	- Locathah: 0 (Indifferent) - Parallel outsiders.
	- Couaxolotl: –1 (Unfriendly) - Obscure figures tied to lost memory.
	- Aventi: 0 (Indifferent) - Occasionally encountered, not interpreted.

#### Ship Rules
Failing pressure fields, compromised compartments, and mishaps create escalating consequences that push encounters out of the ship and into the environment, while ensuring recovery is fast enough to support long-term exploration without attrition spirals.

##### Pressure Fields and Compartments
- Ships are divided into a small number of large, generalized compartments. Each compartment is sealed by a magical pressure field that keeps water out and maintains breathable conditions. Compartments are independent; failure affects only the compromised section.
- Pressure fields are resilient but temporary. They exist to separate travel from combat and to allow partial, escalating failure rather than total loss of the vessel.

##### Field Charge
- Ships track **Charge** per compartment, representing the integrity of the magical pressure field sealing that space. Each compartment begins at maximum Charge; as it takes hits, Charge decrements. When a compartment reaches zero, its pressure field fails and it floods.
- **Decrementing Charge**. Each hit against a compartment decrements Charge by 1. If a single hit exceeds the vessel's **Mishap Threshold**, Charge decrements by 2 instead and triggers a roll on the Mishap table. A standard 1-point decrement does not trigger a Mishap roll.
- **Flooded Compartments**. When a compartment reaches zero Charge, its pressure field collapses. It immediately becomes open underwater terrain — normal underwater movement and combat rules apply within it. Other compartments are unaffected.

##### Repairs and Recovery
- Charge can be restored through repairs, emergency actions, or by expending ship fuel (residuum or processed dragonshards). Each repair action restores 1 Charge to a compartment of the crew's choice. A flooded compartment can be restored the same way, returning it to 1 Charge. Recovery is intentionally fast — ships are pressure valves, not fragile set pieces.

##### Mishaps
- A single d20 Mishap Table governs all ship complications. Most results produce no mishap; the remainder introduce brief but disruptive effects. Mishaps create momentary chaos rather than permanent damage.

| d20  | Mishap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1-12 | **No Mishap**. No additional effect beyond the stress increase.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 13   | **Power Surge**. A violent arc of bound energy lashes through the ship. One random creature inside the ship takes 2d6 force damage.                                                                                                                         |
| 14   | **Pressure Surge**. The ship momentarily compresses under external force. Until the end of the next round, all creatures inside the ship treat movement as difficult terrain.                                                                               |
| 15   | **Thermal Flash**. Extreme heat or cold vents into one compartment. All creatures in that compartment must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or take 2d6 cold or fire damage; on a success, they take half damage.                                     |
| 16   | **Arcane Feedback**. The stabilizing field discharges inward. All creatures currently concentrating inside the ship must immediately make a concentration saving throw.                                                                                     |
| 17   | **Structural Entanglement**. Ice, debris, or a creature lodges against the hull. The ship’s speed becomes 0 until the obstruction is cleared from outside the ship. The ship can still take stress while pinned.                                            |
| 18   | **Seal Jam**. A bulkhead or hatch locks half-open under strain. That opening becomes a narrow choke point: creatures can attack through it, but only one creature can move through it at a time; the area around it is lightly obscured by spray and vapor. |
| 19   | **Intrusion Vector**. A seam, conduit, or maintenance channel ruptures. One hostile creature of appropriate size enters the ship immediately through that point, appearing in a specific compartment.                                                       |
| 20   | **Cascading Instability**. Roll twice on this table and apply both results (ignore further No Mishap results).                                                                                                                                              |

#### Ship Types

##### Elemental Submarines
***Gargantuan Vehicle (60 ft length)***, **Max Charge**: 4 per compartment, **Mishap Threshold**: 15
Designed for sustained undersea travel and high-pressure environments. Four (4) compartments:
- Forward Compartment.  Observation and approach-facing space. Most likely to be affected by rams, ambushes, and frontal pressure.  
- Crew Compartment. Single shared interior space. Any mishap here puts everyone in danger at once.  
- Containment Core. Elemental binding and field generation. Mishaps here skew toward power surges, arcane feedback, and cascading instability.
Because there are only three compartments, repeated mishaps escalate fast. This vessel encourages getting out of the ship early once things start going bad.

##### Seastriders
***Gargantuan Vehicle (40 ft length)***, **Max Charge**: 6 per compartment, **Mishap Threshold**: 10
Built for extreme depths and uneven terrain, slow but brutally stable. Five (5) compartments:
- Central Hull. Main sealed crew space. Hardest to compromise.
- Left Assembly. One side of the walker’s limbs and housing.
- Right Assembly. Mirrored to the left; damage here causes listing or tilt.
- Forward Module. Manipulators, sensors, and terrain-facing systems.
- Rear Module. Power storage and exhaust.
Because the compartments are distributed, mishaps often affect part of the walker instead of the whole thing. This vessel encourages external action: climbing out, clearing obstructions, fighting on the seabed.

##### The Nautilux
***Gargantuan Vehicle (100 ft length)***, **Max Charge**: 8 per compartment, **Mishap Threshold**: 20
Rare hybrid vessel capable of surfacing and terrestrial travel. Four (4) large compartments:
- Upper Compartment. Broad, open interior used differently above and below water. Mishaps here are immediately noticeable and disruptive.
- Main Compartment. The largest internal space; when compromised, it creates chaotic, multi-target danger.
- Lower Compartment. Ballast and conversion mechanisms; failures here affect depth control and orientation.
- Aft Compartment. Engines and steering.
Because compartments are large, a single mishap has a wide impact. This vessel encourages rapid response or retreat, not prolonged internal fighting.

- **Travelling Ship: *The Crosscurrent***
	- A fast, weather-scarred sailing vessel with mismatched sails and a shallow draft that lets her slip into ports others avoid. The hull bears old repairs done with incompatible materials—wood, coral-plating, and unfamiliar alloy—yet she rides currents with uncanny ease. The ship may be found traveling the seas or at any port, as necessary to relay information or help the players.
	- **Rex Scruggs** (CG male human, captain / private sailor). "Cap'n Scruggs" is sun-browned and long-limbed, wearing a battered wide-brim hat and a crooked grin that never quite gives away how much he’s clocking at any moment. He speaks with a lazy southern drawl that reads as unserious until it’s too late to take back a deal. Perched on his shoulder is a small clockwork crustacean, brass-and-glass, its legs ticking softly as it records sound and reacts to situations. Rex claims neutrality, but has a consistent weakness for people being pushed around by larger powers.
	- **Jeremy Jenuwine** (NG male half-elf, first mate / navigator). The ship's first mate is neat, soft-spoken, and perpetually ink-stained, with careful eyes and an unshakable calm under pressure. He handles charts, tides, manifests, and negotiations, often translating Rex’s provocations into workable agreements. His bond with Rex is obvious but understated—shared glances, quiet course corrections, and absolute trust in a crisis. Jeremy believes information is power only if used responsibly, which puts him at odds with nearly every port authority they meet.
	- **Thalos Reefborn** (N male aventi, quartermaster / salvager). Thalos is tall and broad-shouldered, with faintly iridescent skin and eyes that reflect light like water seen from below. He keeps meticulous inventory of cargo and provisions, alongside a personal collection of odd relics—pressure-resistant lenses, humming stones, articulated tools—salvaged from ruins he can’t quite place. Thalos knows he comes from a sunken city, but his people’s history reaches him only in fragments and half-remembered stories that don’t line up. He treats his trinkets as practical tools rather than sacred artifacts, quietly afraid of what he might learn if he ever understood them fully.
	- **The Crew Dynamic**. Rex is the face and risk-taker, Jeremy the conscience and compass, and Thalos the quiet engine that keeps the ship running and profitable. Decisions are made informally, usually on deck, and never by vote—consensus emerges or they wait. None of them fully trusts institutions, but they trust each other completely.
